editorial.headline: Operating Electrical Utilisation Installations, Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers third-party operation of high-, medium-, and low-voltage electrical utilisation installations, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35152 is not about selling electricity or building a power project in the abstract. Its scope is narrower and more operational: the running of electrical utilisation installations by a party other than the facility owner or principal user. The record expressly covers high-voltage, medium-voltage, and low-voltage electrical utilisation installations, so the practical centre of gravity is the professional operation of systems that already sit on the consumption side of electricity use. In plain English, this is the activity of operating electrical facilities for another party, across the voltage bands named in the classification.

That makes the registration logic fairly broad, but still specific. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not reserved only for large operators. A small specialist operator and a larger technical services company can both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the registered activity remains the operation of electrical utilisation installations. The important editorial distinction is that scale openness does not expand the business scope: the code remains tied to operating those installations, not to every commercial activity connected to electricity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the clean national reading is that a foreign-owned company may register this activity up to full foreign ownership. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the consequence is not a mystery category or a restricted-equity setup; on the national investment list, this is an open activity with a full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion under the moratorium data in this record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is marked l4_bali_blocked: false. The reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the honest Bali picture: this is not one of the foreign-owned registrations barred by the Bali moratorium in the supplied record. The right caution is therefore not to invent a local cap or hidden partnership condition, because none is stated here; the Bali-side signal is simply that the activity is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali picture is that this activity is not blocked by the moratorium in the supplied record.
